title: Conditional flow matching for inverse posteriors

items.title: Grönwall inequality with an integrable coefficient
items.statement:
Let $a\le b$, let $A\ge0$, let $u:[a,b]\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous, and let $\ell:[a,b]\to[0,\infty)$ be Lebesgue measurable with $\int_a^b\ell(s)\,ds<\infty$. If
$$u(t)\le A+\int_a^t\ell(s)u(s)\,ds\qquad(a\le t\le b),$$
then
$$u(t)\le A\exp\!\left(\int_a^t\ell(s)\,ds\right)\qquad(a\le t\le b).$$
If instead $u(t)\le A+\int_t^b\ell(s)u(s)\,ds$ for every $t\in[a,b]$, then
$$u(t)\le A\exp\!\left(\int_t^b\ell(s)\,ds\right)\qquad(a\le t\le b).$$

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, §2.4, Lemma 2.7
references.locator: Generalized Grönwall inequality with an integrable nonnegative coefficient; proof by an integrating factor.

references.title: Carnegie Mellon University, ODE existence and uniqueness notes, 2026, Grönwall inequality section
references.locator: Grönwall estimate and its application to continuous dependence for ODEs.

items.axiom_use: The estimate uses Countable Choice and Dependent Choice exactly through the library fundamental theorem for absolutely continuous functions, which represents each absolutely continuous function by the integral of its derivative. The change of variable and inequality are otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Global Lipschitz ODE flows and the C1 density formula
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $T>0$, let $d,m\ge1$, and let $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^d$ be jointly continuous on the product Euclidean domain. Suppose that for every compact $K\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ there are nonnegative Lebesgue-measurable $a_K,L_K\in L^1([0,T])$ such that for almost every $t$, simultaneously for all $y\in K$ and $x,x'\in\mathbb R^d$,
$$|b(t,0,y)|\le a_K(t),\qquad |b(t,x,y)-b(t,x',y)|\le L_K(t)|x-x'|.$$
Here $L^1([0,T])$ means the functions have finite Lebesgue integral of their absolute values. Then for every $x_0\in\mathbb R^d$ and $y\in\mathbb R^m$ there is a unique continuously differentiable solution $x_y(\cdot;x_0)$ of
$$\dot x(t)=b(t,x(t),y),\qquad x(0)=x_0,$$
on all of $[0,T]$. Its terminal map $T_y(x_0):=x_y(T;x_0)$ is a bijection with jointly continuous forward and inverse maps in $(x_0,y)$, and for all $x_0,x_1$ and $y\in K$,
$$|T_y(x_0)-T_y(x_1)|\le e^{\int_0^T L_K(t)dt}|x_0-x_1|,\qquad |T_y^{-1}(x_0)-T_y^{-1}(x_1)|\le e^{\int_0^T L_K(t)dt}|x_0-x_1|.$$

In the separate C$^1$ clause, suppose additionally that the state derivative $D_xb$ exists and is jointly continuous. Then for fixed $y$, $T_y$ is a bijection and both $T_y$ and its inverse are continuously differentiable. For a measurable map $S$ and a measure $\mu$, define its image measure by $S_{\#}\mu(E):=\mu(S^{-1}(E))$. The derivative $A_y(t,x_0):=D_{x_0}x_y(t;x_0)$ solves
$$\dot A_y(t,x_0)=D_xb(t,x_y(t;x_0),y)A_y(t,x_0),\qquad A_y(0,x_0)=I_d,$$
with Liouville formula
$$\det A_y(t,x_0)=\exp\!\left(\int_0^t\operatorname{tr}D_xb(s,x_y(s;x_0),y)\,ds\right).$$
Consequently, if a probability measure $\eta$ on $\mathbb R^d$ has Lebesgue density $q$, meaning $\eta(E)=\int_Eq(x)\,dx$ for Borel $E$, the image measure $T_y{}_{\#}\eta$ has density
$$z\longmapsto q(T_y^{-1}(z))\,|\det D T_y^{-1}(z)|.$$
The global Lipschitz clause alone gives a bi-Lipschitz flow and does not assert a Jacobian density formula.

references.title: Gerald Teschl, Ordinary Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems, §§2.3–2.6
references.locator: §2.3 Corollary 2.6 for an integrable time-dependent global Lipschitz coefficient; §2.4 Lemma 2.7 for generalized Grönwall and C1 dependence; §2.6 for global continuation. The local proof supplies the construction and estimates used here.

references.title: Carnegie Mellon University, ODE existence and uniqueness notes, 2026
references.locator: ODE existence, Grönwall continuous-dependence, flow and Liouville formula sections; used as a second lecture-note treatment, with the integrable-coefficient extension proved locally here.

references.title: Gerald B. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorem 2.47
references.locator: C1 change-of-variables formula for nonnegative Lebesgue-measurable functions.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are used through the integrable- coefficient Grönwall lemma for the flow bounds. Countable Choice is also required by the C1 change-of-variables theorem in the optional density clause. No full Axiom of Choice is used here.

items.title: An exact triangular transport disintegrates to the posterior
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\pi$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$, where $d,m\ge1$, and let $\pi_Y(B):=\pi(\mathbb R^d\times B)$ be its second marginal. Let $\eta$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$, and let $y\mapsto\pi_y$ be a probability kernel satisfying
$$\pi(A\times B)=\int_B\pi_y(A)\,\pi_Y(dy)$$
for all Borel $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ and $B\subseteq\mathbb R^m$. Suppose $T:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$ is Borel and triangular, $T(x,y)=(T_y(x),y)$, with each $T_y$ a Borel bijection, and define the image measure by $T_{\#}\mu(E):=\mu(T^{-1}(E))$. If
$$T_{\#}(\eta\otimes\pi_Y)=\pi,$$
then $T_y{}_{\#}\eta=\pi_y$ as probability measures for $\pi_Y$-almost every $y$. By disintegration on standard Borel spaces, such a kernel $\pi_y$ exists and is unique outside one $\pi_Y$-null set. In a proper Bayesian model, when $\pi$ is the joint parameter/data law, this conditional kernel is the posterior kernel; the conclusion says an exact triangular transport maps the reference law to the data-conditioned posterior for almost every datum.

For the triangular terminal flow in the preceding ODE lemma, joint continuity supplies the Borel map and each fiber is a bijection. The theorem requires only the exact joint pushforward identity; it does not require a density or a Jacobian formula.

references.title: Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, 5th ed.
references.locator: Regular conditional distributions and disintegration for standard Borel variables; the local proof supplies the rectangle identity and common-null-set uniqueness interfaces used here.

references.title: S. R. S. Varadhan, Probability Theory, Chapter 4
references.locator: Conditional distributions, disintegration and conditional integration for standard Borel spaces.

items.axiom_use: The Axiom of Choice is required by the standard-Borel disintegration supplier for existence and simultaneous almost-everywhere uniqueness of the conditional posterior kernel. The pushforward and Tonelli calculations are choice-free once the kernels are supplied. The ODE flow supplier uses only Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, both consequences of AC.

items.title: Conditional flow matching for inverse posteriors
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d,m,n,B\ge1$, let $\eta$ be a reference probability on $\mathbb R^d$, and let $\pi$ be the proper joint law of an unknown $X_1\in\mathbb R^d$ and data $Y\in\mathbb R^m$ in a specified Bayesian inverse model. Write $\pi_Y$ for the data marginal and $\pi_y$ for a posterior-kernel version of the conditional law of $X_1$ given $Y=y$. Assume
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m}|x_1|^2\,\pi(dx_1,dy)+\int_{\mathbb R^d}|x_0|^2\,\eta(dx_0)<\infty.$$
Choose a jointly measurable parameterized vector-field family $v_\theta:[0,1]\times\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^d$, with parameter set $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ for some $p\ge1$, whose candidates have finite population squared loss under the training law below.

**Declared inputs.** Supply independent sampling routines for $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$, $\eta$, and $\pi$; here $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$ is Lebesgue probability on the unit interval. Supply an initialiser $\mathrm{Init}$ returning a parameter in $\Theta$ or failure; an optimizer update callable $\mathrm{Update}(k,\theta,\widehat{\mathcal L}_n,\mathcal D_n)$ returning a parameter in $\Theta$ or failure, with each call counting as one optimizer step; a named statistic callable $S(k,\theta,\widehat{\mathcal L}_n,\mathcal D_n)$ returning a finite real value when evaluation succeeds; a finite step budget $M\ge1$ and tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm opt}>0$; a flow-check callable; and a numerical ODE solver with a declared finite step or tolerance budget $h$. Every callable must return its specified value or a failure status in finite time. Any randomization used by these callables is part of the declared input.

**Training and optimizer instructions.** Draw $n$ independent triples
$$(t_i,X_{0i},(X_{1i},Y_i))\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\otimes\eta\otimes\pi,$$
and form $X_{t_i}=(1-t_i)X_{0i}+t_iX_{1i}$ and $V_i=X_{1i}-X_{0i}$. Let $\mathcal D_n=((t_i,X_{t_i},Y_i,V_i))_{i=1}^n$ and evaluate the empirical squared loss
$$\widehat{\mathcal L}_n(\theta)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl|v_\theta(t_i,X_{t_i},Y_i)-V_i\bigr|^2.$$
If sampling fails, return **sampling-failed**. Otherwise call $\mathrm{Init}$; if it fails or returns a parameter outside $\Theta$, return **optimizer-failed** with no fitted field. Set $k=0$ and repeat the following steps in order: evaluate $\widehat{\mathcal L}_n(\theta_k)$ and $S(k,\theta_k,\widehat{\mathcal L}_n,\mathcal D_n)$; if either evaluation fails or either value is nonfinite, return **optimizer-failed** with no fitted field; if $S\le\varepsilon_{\rm opt}$, stop with status **converged**; if $k=M$, stop with status **budget-exhausted**; otherwise call $\mathrm{Update}(k,\theta_k,\widehat{\mathcal L}_n,\mathcal D_n)$, returning **optimizer-failed** with no fitted field if the call fails, returns a parameter outside $\Theta$, or yields a nonfinite value, and then set $\theta_{k+1}$ to its output and increase $k$ by one. For either successful stopping status, return $\widehat v=v_{\theta_k}$, its achieved training loss, the last value of $S$, $k$, $M$, $\varepsilon_{\rm opt}$ and the optimizer status. A finite-data stopping status does not certify $\widehat v=v^*$.

The population least-squares target is the conditional-expectation class
$$v^*(t,x,y)=\mathbb E[X_1-X_0\mid\sigma(t,X_t,Y)]$$
coordinatewise, evaluated at $(t,x,y)$ through a chosen measurable representative. A conditional expectation is only an almost-sure equivalence class, so this formula does not specify an off-support pointwise extension.

**Flow and sampling instructions.** For a query datum $y$, call the flow checker on $\widehat v$ and the data-parameter domain containing $y$. It returns **pass** only when it certifies all hypotheses of the ODE flow lemma, including joint continuity and the integrable global spatial-Lipschitz and origin-growth bounds on compact data-parameter sets containing $y$. If it does not return pass, return **field-regularity-failed** with the optimizer record and no terminal samples. Otherwise, for $j=1,\ldots,B$, draw independent $Z_0^j\sim\eta$ and call the declared solver to integrate on $0\le t\le1$
$$\dot Z_t^j=\widehat v(t,Z_t^j,y),\qquad Z_0^j,$$
with budget $h$. Record the returned finite endpoint as the terminal approximation $\widehat Z_1^j$ only when the solver reports success; treat a success response with a nonfinite endpoint as a failed integration. Also record each status and any certified solver error estimate, marking an unavailable estimate unquantified. Continue through all $B$ calls after a solver failure. Return the successful terminal approximations and all per-call records, together with the field and optimizer records; the overall status is **completed** if every integration succeeds and **solver-failed** otherwise. A sampling-call failure returns **sampling-failed** and the records collected so far.

If the exact triangular flow of $\widehat v$ were known to satisfy $T_{\#}(\eta\otimes\pi_Y)=\pi$, the exact transport theorem would imply $T_y{}_{\#}\eta=\pi_y$ for $\pi_Y$-almost every $y$. Finite regression loss, optimizer termination, and solver success alone do not establish this joint pushforward identity or exact posterior sampling. Record posterior model, discretization, kernel, burn-in, Monte Carlo and solver components under the declared posterior-computation error budget when applicable. The budget does not supply a learned-flow regression or optimizer-error estimate; report those separately as measured or certified quantities, and mark unavailable quantities unquantified rather than zero.

items.axiom_use: AC supplies the conditional-expectation L2 projection and standard-Borel posterior kernel interfaces. Its consequences Countable Choice and Dependent Choice supply the ODE-flow and density clauses when their stated regularity hypotheses hold. No claim that finite-sample fitting or numerical integration is exact is made.

items.title: Population regression and exact-flow meaning of conditional flow matching
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d,m,n\ge1$, let $\eta$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$, and let $\pi$ be a proper Bayesian joint law on $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^m$ with data marginal $\pi_Y$ and posterior-kernel version $\pi_y$. Assume $\int|x_0|^2\eta(dx_0)+\int|x_1|^2\pi(dx_1,dy)<\infty$. Let $t$, $X_0$ and $(X_1,Y)$ be independent with law $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\otimes\eta\otimes\pi$, where $X_t=(1-t)X_0+tX_1$, and $V=X_1-X_0$ has finite second moment. Write $\mathcal L(v):=\mathbb E|v(t,X_t,Y)-V|^2$ and let $\widehat{\mathcal L}_n(v)$ be the empirical mean of this squared residual over $n\ge1$ independent training triples. Then the conditional-expectation class $v^*(t,X_t,Y)=\mathbb E[V\mid\sigma(t,X_t,Y)]$ admits a measurable representative in $(t,x,y)$ and uniquely minimizes $\mathcal L$ over square-integrable predictors measurable in these coordinates, up to almost-sure equality. For every fixed measurable candidate $v$ with finite population loss,
$$\mathbb E[\widehat{\mathcal L}_n(v)]=\mathcal L(v).$$
This expectation identity is for a fixed candidate, not a data-dependent fitted field.

If a fitted field satisfies all hypotheses of the global ODE flow lemma, it has an exact triangular terminal map $T(x,y)=(T_y(x),y)$. If also $T_{\#}(\eta\otimes\pi_Y)=\pi$, then $T_y{}_{\#}\eta=\pi_y$ as probability measures outside one $\pi_Y$-null set. These conclusions make no assertion that finite training or numerical solver success establishes the exact joint pushforward identity.

references.title: Blechschmidt et al., section 3.2 and Theorem 3.1

items.axiom_use: AC supplies the conditional-expectation L2 projection and standard-Borel posterior kernel interfaces. items.title: Dimension-uniform conditional flow error for function-valued Bayesian posteriors
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Its implications supply Dependent Choice and Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional ODE flow assumptions.

Let $\mathcal H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be compact, and let $y\mapsto\Pi^y$ be the pointwise potential posterior of a proper Bayesian inverse model, with positive finite evidence and finite second moment for every $y\in K$. Let $P_n$ be finite-rank orthogonal projections on $\mathcal H$ with $P_nx\to x$ for every $x\in\mathcal H$, let $\mathcal H_n=P_n\mathcal H$, and let $\Pi_n^y$ be proper posteriors defined by declared finite-rank forward/potential approximations on $\mathcal H_n$, with finite second moments for every $y\in K$. Write $i_n:\mathcal H_n\hookrightarrow\mathcal H$ for inclusion and define the posterior model error
$$e_{\mathrm{post},n}:=\sup_{y\in K}W_{2,\mathcal H}(i_{n\#}\Pi_n^y,\Pi^y),$$
where $W_{2,\mathcal H}(\mu,\nu)$ is the infimum, over joint laws with marginals $\mu,\nu$, of the square root of the expected squared Hilbert distance. This term includes both posterior-potential and finite-rank model error; the known Hellinger potential/discretization estimates would need an explicit moment or tail argument to control it in $W_2$.

Let $\pi$ be the prior-predictive joint law of $(X_1,Y)$ and assume the global prior-predictive moment condition
$$\int_{\mathcal H\times\mathbb R^m}\|x_1\|_{\mathcal H}^2\,\pi(dx_1,dy)<\infty.$$
Let $\eta$ be an independent reference probability on $\mathcal H$ with finite second moment, and use the product training law $\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\otimes\eta\otimes\pi$. Let $X_t=(1-t)X_0+tX_1$ and let $v^*(t,X_t,Y)=\mathbb E[X_1-X_0\mid\sigma(t,X_t,Y)]$ be a chosen continuum conditional regression version. For projected endpoints, define
$$v_n^*(t,P_nX_t,Y)=\mathbb E[P_n(X_1-X_0)\mid\sigma(t,P_nX_t,Y)]$$
and the finite-rank conditional-target discrepancy
$$e_{\mathrm{target},n}:=\sup_{y\in K}\left(\int_0^1\mathbb E\!\left[\left\|P_nv^*(t,X_t,y)-v_n^*(t,P_nX_t,y)\right\|_{\mathcal H}^2\mid Y=y\right]dt\right)^{1/2}.$$
The conditional expectation versions at $Y=y$ must be chosen on all $y\in K$ for these suprema. For a measurable vector field $v:\,[0,1]\times\mathcal H_n\times K\to\mathcal H_n$, define its pointwise conditional population loss by
$$\mathcal L_{n,y}(v):=\int_0^1\mathbb E\!\left[\left\|v(t,P_nX_t,y)-P_n(X_1-X_0)\right\|_{\mathcal H}^2\mid Y=y\right]dt,$$
using the selected conditional-law version. For a finite training sample of size $N$, let $\bar v_{n,N}$ be an empirical-risk minimizer in the specified vector-field class, when it exists. On realizations where the declared optimizer returns a field (status **converged** or **budget-exhausted**), let $\widehat v_{n,N}$ be that field; the optimizer-failed case has no learned field and is outside this formulation. Define the uniform conditional statistical and optimizer excess-risk terms by
$$e_{\mathrm{stat},n,N}^2:=\sup_{y\in K}\left[\mathcal L_{n,y}(\bar v_{n,N})-\inf_{v\in\mathcal V_n}\mathcal L_{n,y}(v)\right],\qquad e_{\mathrm{opt},n,N}^2:=\sup_{y\in K}\left[\mathcal L_{n,y}(\widehat v_{n,N})-\mathcal L_{n,y}(\bar v_{n,N})\right]_+$$
where $\mathcal V_n$ is the chosen class and $\mathcal L_{n,y}$ is its population conditional squared regression loss at datum $y$. Let $e_{\mathrm{solver},n,N,h}$ be a certified $W_2$ coupling bound between the numerical endpoint law at solver budget $h$ and the exact learned-flow endpoint law. Finally, let $\Lambda$ be a proposed bound, uniform in $n$ and $y\in K$, for the time-integrated spatial Lipschitz constants of the learned drifts.

Find checkable assumptions under which the learned finite-rank flow defines a posterior sampler $\widehat\Pi_{n,N,h}^y$ and, for each training realization satisfying explicit risk certificates (or with a stated probability over training data), satisfies a dimension-uniform bound of the form
$$\sup_{y\in K}W_{2,\mathcal H}(i_{n\#}\widehat\Pi_{n,N,h}^y,\Pi^y)\le e_{\mathrm{post},n}+e_{\mathrm{solver},n,N,h}+C e^{\Lambda}\bigl(e_{\mathrm{target},n}+e_{\mathrm{stat},n,N}+e_{\mathrm{opt},n,N}\bigr),$$
with $C$ independent of $n$. The result should derive usable bounds for the posterior model term from the Bayesian potential and discretization hypotheses, establish the uniform-in-$y$ training terms from prior-predictive data, and state the required flow regularity and numerical coupling assumptions. It must not assume that a finite-sample learned field or numerical solver already has the exact joint pushforward property; that property is the conclusion to be certified through the displayed error terms.

items.axiom_use: Assume AC for standard-Borel posterior disintegration and the conditional- expectation versions in the formulation; AC implies Dependent Choice and Countable Choice, the choice prerequisites of the finite-dimensional ODE supplier. This is an open problem, not a proved supplier or an axiom branch used to establish another item.

title: Conditional flow matching for inverse posteriors — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Accurate posterior means with low independent-MH acceptance
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the general density-based Metropolis–Hastings interface. In the stationary-diffusion inverse-problem experiment with $m=256$ observations, noise variance $\gamma^2=10^{-5}$, and $n_{KL}=128$ prior modes, use the baseline conditional-flow-matching MLP with 800 hidden units. The reported flow-matching independent-Metropolis–Hastings acceptance rates for four different true parameters are respectively $0.66\%$, $11.21\%$, $5.97\%$, and $5.47\%$. In this same experiment, the reported posterior means and 95\% bands agree with the DRAM reference to between $0.8\%$ and $1.8\%$ in relative $L^2$. The first truth is a prior-predictive tail observation: its normalized radius is $2.53$, the median training radius is $0.85$, and only $0.12\%$ of the two million training observations have a larger radius. This reported case shows that close posterior means and bands do not by themselves imply high independent-Metropolis–Hastings acceptance or establish full posterior accuracy.

references.title: Jan Blechschmidt, Oliver G. Ernst, Moritz Poguntke, and Björn Sprungk, Flow Matching for Fast Posterior Sampling in Bayesian Inverse Problems
references.locator: §4.2.1, Fig. 6 and Table 1 (PDF pp. 15–16): $m=256$, noise variance $10^{-5}$, $n_{KL}=128$, baseline MLP with 800 hidden units and four FM-IMH acceptance rates; §4.2.2, normalized observation radii and prior-predictive training-tail frequencies; §4.2.1, relative $L^2$ comparison of posterior means and 95% bands with DRAM.

items.axiom_use: The reported experiment is empirical. AC is required only by the general density-based Metropolis–Hastings interface used to interpret its correction; no theorem that the observed finite-run summaries equal the posterior is asserted.

items.title: Likelihood-free conditional flow matching without an MH correction
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let a proper prior and forward simulator define a joint prior-predictive law $\pi$ for an unknown $X_1$ and data $Y$. Suppose the available interface can draw independent pairs $(X_1,Y)\sim\pi$ and reference states $X_0\sim\eta$, but supplies neither an evaluable likelihood density $L(x_1;y)$ nor an auxiliary nonnegative random estimate $\widehat L(x_1;y,U)$ with $\mathbb E_U\widehat L(x_1;y,U)=L(x_1;y)$, where the expectation is over auxiliary randomness $U$. Conditional flow matching can train from these joint and reference samples and an independent $t\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]$ using the linear path $X_t=(1-t)X_0+tX_1$ and target velocity $X_1-X_0$, without evaluating $L$. For a fixed query datum $y$, suppose the finite-dimensional prior has a finite-valued Lebesgue density $p_0$ with respect to the sigma-finite Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ on the standard-Borel state space $\mathbb R^d$ equipped with its Borel sigma-algebra. Assume the model has a finite-valued measurable likelihood density $L(\cdot;y)$ at this datum, and set $\widetilde p_y(x)=p_0(x)L(x;y)$. Require $0<Z_y:=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\widetilde p_y(x)\,\lambda(dx)<\infty$, so the posterior is a proper target with finite-valued density $p_y=\widetilde p_y/Z_y$. Suppose the reference law $\eta$ has a Lebesgue density and the learned flow satisfies the separate C$^1$ hypotheses of the ODE lemma; let $q_y$ be a finite-valued measurable version of the resulting proposal density, with $\int q_y\,d\lambda=1$. Its independent proposal kernel is $Q_y(x,A):=\int_Aq_y(z)\,\lambda(dz)$ for every $x$ and Borel $A$. For pairs with positive forward proposal-flow density $\widetilde p_y(x)q_y(z)$, the density-based independent-Metropolis–Hastings acceptance probability is
$$\alpha_y(x,z)=\min\!\left\{1,\frac{\widetilde p_y(z)q_y(x)}{\widetilde p_y(x)q_y(z)}\right\}.$$
The stated sampling interface does not in general supply this ratio, so it does not by itself give an evaluable density-based correction. In a specified special model the likelihood ratio may cancel or be otherwise known without separate likelihood evaluations; such a case needs no missing likelihood oracle. This example concerns the general limitation of the specified density-based correction; it does not rule out pseudo-marginal correction if an appropriate likelihood estimator is supplied, nor other correction methods with different inputs.

references.title: Jan Blechschmidt, Oliver G. Ernst, Moritz Poguntke, and Björn Sprungk, Flow Matching for Fast Posterior Sampling in Bayesian Inverse Problems
references.locator: §3.1–§3.2, especially Remark 3.1 (PDF pp. 5–9): conditional training and sampling use joint prior-predictive samples without likelihood evaluation; §3.3–§3.4 and §4.4: independent-MH correction and diagnostics require an unnormalized posterior density, and the stochastic Lotka–Volterra example has no likelihood.

references.title: Art B. Owen, Monte Carlo Theory, Methods and Examples, Chapter 11 §11.4
references.locator: Independent Metropolis–Hastings accepts by the target-to-proposal density ratio, which requires an evaluable unnormalized target density when used for a correction.

items.axiom_use: AC is required for the general conditional-posterior and density-based Metropolis–Hastings interfaces; its implications DC and Countable Choice supply the ODE-flow prerequisites. The stated simulator interface makes no likelihood evaluation or unbiased likelihood estimator available; it does not rule out a different interface that supplies such an estimator.
